content.chapter: Chapter 1 — A Green Plan for Europe
objectives: Say what the Green Deal is.
Use wants and says.
Say how they use less.
content.pedagogy: Grammar is found in the story first. Learners notice the form in a story sentence, then use it about their own life. With young learners (Years 2–4), teach the Language Focus as chunks: say, repeat, act and play.
content.grammarFocus: present simple with -s for one thing (works, wants, says); many things without -s (make, send).
content.lessonPlan: 0–5 Show a map of Europe. Ask: “What countries do you know?” 5–10 Listen: “What is the name of the plan?” 10–17 Read. Learners find two dates (2019, 2050). 17–20 Quick Challenge. 20–27 Language Focus. 27–30 Say It. The audio for A1 is not ready yet: read the chapter aloud yourself, slowly, twice.
discussionPoints: The plan says, “Use less, and throw away less.” What can you use less at home?
interactiveTips: Tap the two hotspots on the picture before the Quick Challenge.
Word Notes: plan, factory, air, gas, net zero, throw away.
Before reading, teach “group”, “countries” and “world” with a map.
Net zero is a big idea. Draw two arrows: gas into the air, gas out of the air. Same size = net zero.

differentiation.strugglingLearners: Give the frames “At home, I use less …” and “I can use my old … again.”
differentiation.fastFinishers: Learners say why bad gases are a problem.

classroomManagement.monitoring: Check the -s: The EU wants, the plan says. Many things: cars send, gases make.

rubricLevels.secure: Chooses works and says for one thing.
rubricLevels.notYet: Say “The EU …” and point to one finger.

rubricLevels.secure: Says what the Green Deal is.

noteTaking.focus: After reading, learners write one or two words in each box.
noteTaking.afterNotes: From the notes, learners say two sentences about the chapter.

mediationTasks.translation: Learners say the chapter’s key sentence in their home language.
mediationTasks.homeRetell: Learners tell the chapter to someone at home in their home language.

objectives: Name the three big goals.

content.pedagogy: Grammar is found in the story first. Learners notice the form in a story sentence, then use it about their own life. With young learners (Years 2–4), teach the Language Focus as chunks: say, repeat, act and play.
content.grammarFocus: should / should not + verb; is getting + -er (getting hotter); too many / too much.
content.lessonPlan: 0–5 Draw a tree, a factory and a coin on the board. Ask: “What are these?” 5–10 Listen: “How many goals are there?” 10–17 Read. Learners match each goal with a picture. 17–20 Quick Challenge. 20–27 Language Focus. 27–30 Write It. The audio for A1 is not ready yet: read the chapter aloud yourself, slowly, twice.
discussionPoints: Plants and animals need a safe home. How can we help them?
interactiveTips: Tap the two hotspots on the picture before the Quick Challenge.
Word Notes: goal, climate, nature, company.
Before reading, teach “goal” with a football picture: a goal is something you want.
55% = more than half. Show it with 100 dots on the board.

differentiation.strugglingLearners: Give the frames “We should …” and “We should not …”.

content.chapter: Chapter 3 — Why Do We Need It?
objectives: Say why the Green Deal is important.
Use there is and there are.
Talk about their town.
content.pedagogy: Grammar is found in the story first. Learners notice the form in a story sentence, then use it about their own life. With young learners (Years 2–4), teach the Language Focus as chunks: say, repeat, act and play.
content.grammarFocus: there is / there are; there will be; past simple used (For many years, people used …).
content.lessonPlan: 0–5 Show a picture of a dirty river. Ask: “Is it clean?” 5–10 Listen: “Is our world in danger?” 10–17 Read. 17–20 Quick Challenge. 20–27 Language Focus. 27–30 Say It. Group Task: Problems and Answers. The audio for A1 is not ready yet: read the chapter aloud yourself, slowly, twice.
discussionPoints: Cars, homes and factories use energy every day. How do you use energy every day?
interactiveTips: Tap the two hotspots on the picture before the Quick Challenge.
Word Notes: danger, pollution, oil, coal, energy, war.
Before reading, teach “weather”, “expensive” and “on time” with pictures.
Wars: talk about it simply. Do not ask learners about wars or their own families.

differentiation.strugglingLearners: Give the frames “In my town, there is …” and “There are a lot of …”.
differentiation.fastFinishers: Learners say why energy is expensive today.

classroomManagement.instructions: Read. Find three things people use for energy.
checkQuestions: What are they? (oil, gas and coal)
classroomManagement.monitoring: Check there is + one thing or pollution; there are + wars, cars.

rubricLevels.notYet: Hold up one finger (is) and two fingers (are).

rubricLevels.secure: Says two problems from the chapter.

content.pedagogy: Grammar is found in the story first. Learners notice the form in a story sentence, then use it about their own life. With young learners (Years 2–4), teach the Language Focus as chunks: say, repeat, act and play.
content.grammarFocus: there will be; can + verb (can be, can make); superlative the best.
content.lessonPlan: 0–5 Show a battery and a picture of a solar panel. Ask: “What do they do?” 5–10 Listen: “What can factories make?” 10–17 Read. 17–20 Quick Challenge. 20–27 Language Focus. 27–30 Say It. The audio for A1 is not ready yet: read the chapter aloud yourself, slowly, twice.

interactiveTips: Tap the two hotspots on the picture before the Quick Challenge.

The name of the law stays in English: the Net-Zero Industry Act. Learners do not need to learn it by heart.

metadata.title: The European Green Deal A1 — Teacher Guide
metadata.subtitle: 8 short lessons with chapter-specific support, grammar found in the story, and 30-minute lesson plans
metadata.estimatedDuration: 8 chapter lessons of about 30 minutes each, plus one 40-minute review lesson for the end pages.
metadata.targetAudience: A1 English learners: young beginners (Years 2–4) and adult beginners.
metadata.targetLearners: Learners who can read very short, simple sentences with pictures, sentence frames and help from the teacher.
metadata.purpose: Develop A1 reading, listening, speaking and writing through the European Green Deal: clean energy, less waste, new rules, smart shopping and working together for our world.
metadata.approachDesc: Route in every chapter: Before You Read → Listen → Read → Quick Challenge → Language Focus (Look → Practise → Use) → I can. Grammar is found in the story first. Learners notice the form in a story sentence, then use it about their own life.

readingFramework.before: Before You Read: one picture or one guess question.
readingFramework.during: The audio for A1 is not ready yet: read the chapter aloud yourself, slowly, twice. Then learners read and do one small task (underline, columns, act).
readingFramework.after: Quick Challenge, then Language Focus (Look → Practise → Use), then I can and an exit ticket.

cefrProfile.intro: This book is written for CEFR A1. The table shows the A1 descriptors of the CEFR Companion Volume (2020) that the tasks are built on. Vocabulary (English Vocabulary Profile): learners see only A1 words, words with a Word Note and words from the story. Instruction words that the app uses in every book (match, order, true, false, chapter) are taught once in the first lesson. Grammar (English Grammar Profile): present simple, present continuous, there is / there are, can and imperatives are A1. Should / should not, mustn’t, will, comparatives (cheaper, hotter) and the best are A2. The text uses them, so learners meet them in the text and choose them in exercises. Free use is only expected with sentence frames. Türkiye Century Maarif Model English Curriculum (Years 2–8): “CEFR level A1 has been adapted as A1.1, A1.2, A1.3 in Years 2, 3 and 4 for Primary Education.” The topic of this book is close to Year 4, Theme 5 (dangers for sea animals: plastic, waste, pollution, climate change). The language chunks this book supports from that theme are should / shouldn’t, mustn’t and will. The curriculum’s learning outcomes are written for its own themes. This book is a supplementary reader, so it supports these language chunks but does not cover a theme’s outcomes. Young learners (Years 2–4): the curriculum says “There is no analysis or teaching of grammatical structures at this stage.” With children, teach each Language Focus as chunks: say, repeat, act and play. Do not read the Explanation lines to them. The Explanation lines are for adult beginners and for self-study.

rows.descriptor: Can understand very short, simple texts a single phrase at a time, picking up familiar names, words and basic phrases and rereading as required.
practice: Before You Read and Quick Challenge in every chapter.

rows.descriptor: Can ask and answer simple questions, initiate and respond to simple statements in areas of immediate need or on very familiar topics.
practice: Chapter 3: talk about your town with there is / there are.
Chapter 6: agree on class rules with mustn’t.

rows.descriptor: Can produce simple, mainly isolated phrases about people and places.
practice: Chapter 3: show the “Problems and Answers” poster.
Chapter 6: read the class repair list.

rows.descriptor: Can give information about matters of personal relevance (e.g. likes and dislikes, family, pets) using simple words/signs and basic expressions. Can produce simple isolated phrases and sentences.
practice: Chapter 2: write good ideas for nature.
Chapter 8: write how we can help.

rows.descriptor: Can understand instructions addressed carefully and slowly to them and follow short, simple directions.
practice: Instruction check questions in every chapter (Classroom management).

sensitiveNotes.title: Source fidelity and respectful teaching
notes: This is an information text, not a story. The numbers and dates come from official EU and Turkish sources (see the book’s references). Do not change them.
Chapter 3 mentions wars. Talk about it simply and do not ask learners about wars or their families.
Climate change can worry young learners. End each lesson with something learners can do (use less, repair, recycle).
Do not add numbers, dates or details that are not in this A1 book.

grammarSequence: Chapter 1: present simple with -s for one thing (works, wants, says); many things without -s (make, send).
Chapter 2: should / should not + verb; is getting + -er (getting hotter); too many / too much.
Chapter 3: there is / there are; there will be; past simple used (For many years, people used …).
Chapter 4: comparative -er (cheaper, hotter); need + noun; never.
Chapter 5: there will be; can + verb (can be, can make); superlative the best.
Chapter 6: mustn’t + verb (a rule); can + verb; soon there will be.
Chapter 7: before + sentence; then; present continuous (Jobs are changing).
Chapter 8: past simple made vs. present wants / has; should; can.

miniProject.title: Review lesson (40 minutes)
miniProject.desc: Knowledge Check (10 min), Vocabulary Challenge (5 min), Language Review (15 min), Final Challenge (10 min). Mediation task: Learners explain the energy label on a real machine at home (a fridge or a washing machine) to a family member in their home language. Reading diary: “My favorite chapter is … because …”

metadata.subtitle: Look • Read • Words • Check
metadata.estimatedStudyTime: About 15 minutes per chapter, plus the review pages at the end
metadata.whoIsThisFor: A1 learners who read the book about the European Green Deal at home or on their own.
learningGoals: Read the 8 short chapters of the book about the European Green Deal.
Learn the Word Notes of each chapter.
Use should, mustn’t, can and there will be in your own sentences.
recommendedUse: The audio is not ready yet. Read each chapter two times, one time aloud.
Do the end pages after Chapter 8.

readingDiary.intro: Write short answers when you finish the book.
prompts: One new word I want to keep:
One thing I can do for our world:

sections.title: 1. Make Your Plan
sections.text: This book has 8 short chapters. One chapter takes about 15 minutes.
points: Before each chapter, read its “I can” lines.

sections.title: 2. Every Chapter: 4 Steps
sections.text: Do the same four steps in every chapter.
points: Look and guess: Look at the picture. Answer “Before You Read”.
Read: Read the chapter two times. Read it aloud one time.
Words: Tap the bold words. Say each word two times.
Check: Do the Quick Challenge and the Language Focus. Then read “I can”. Can you do it?

sections.title: 3. Look Back
sections.text: At the end of the book:
points: Do the end pages: Knowledge Check, Vocabulary Challenge, Language Review, Final Challenge.
Which chapter did you like? Why?
Tell someone in your family about the three big goals in your home language.
